A small fish with 31-33 plates along its body. The body is vertically flattened and the tail is very slim. The males are slightly taller than the females. This fish has a pointed mouth which opens at an upward slanted angle.

The species exhibits a relatively large head, with its body tapering to a flattened form towards the posterior. Its eyes are prominently bulging and situated close together. It inhabits the muddy substrates of coastal areas or estuarine environments. Utilizing its pectoral fins, it navigates the mudflat by hopping, preying on small crustaceans and insects.

Silver Prochilodus are medium-sized freshwater fish found in Edania. Their silvery bodies gleam with a hint of turquoise, and they're easy to spot thanks to the four or five bold black stripes along their sides. These fish stick together in schools, usually foraging near the riverbed for algae and bits of organic debris.
A distinctive feature of this fish is the silver stripe running horizontally along its side. Known for traveling in schools, they are often caught in large quantities using nets.

A skipjack has a thick, chubby, spindle-shaped body with a blue-black back and a glossy silver abdomen. It features 4 to 10 black horizontal stripes, which are difficult to discern when the fish is alive.
Its body size is thin and less than a span. It is darker on the back, and white on the stomach. It spawns in the pebble bed under the shallow water of a stream in late spring, after which it dies.
This fish has a flat and small head with large eyes. The body coloration is a light brown on the back, with a distinct black spot in front of the dorsal fin, while the other fins lack any spots.

The spined bittering is a freshwater fish known to inhabit midstream and downstream sections of rivers, particularly where the riverbed is covered with mud. These areas are characterized by slow-moving water, making it easier to spot this species. It typically measures around 10cm in length and features a body that is notably flattened on both sides. Its strikingly colorful scales make it a distinctive presence in freshwater environments, allowing for easy identification.

This fish resembles the mudfish, yet can be easily identified by the distinct spots on its sides. It typically inhabits the midstream areas of rivers or regions covered in sand. Its diet consists of algae and small insects. While it is edible, it is not particularly flavorful.
There have been cases of kids on Iliya Island who love squid diving into the water to catch their quarry, only to come out with ink on their faces.

Starfish, despite their charming star-shaped appearance, possess remarkable regenerative abilities. When a starfish is severed, the detached part can regenerate into a new starfish. However, they are rarely consumed as food due to the overpowering odor they emit upon decay.
A cold sea fish that inhabits between rocks and seaweed.

These fish typically swim in schools and feed on small organisms and fish eggs attached to water plants or the floor. They differ significantly in appearance from common crucian carps, having a lower and more elongated body. Due to the high risk of parasite infestation, consuming them raw is extremely dangerous.

The striped catfish is distinguished by its four pairs of whiskers surrounding its mouth, leading to frequent confusion with the common catfish.

This species predominantly inhabits the shallow waters and rocky areas around Iliya Island. Its first dorsal fin and pectoral fin contain venomous spines, posing a significant threat to fishers and divers alike.

These fish inhabit areas with large stones and pebbles in clear streams. They are nocturnal creatures, hiding beneath stones during the day and feeding on aquatic insects at night. As a native species of Kamasylvia, there have been no recorded instances of them being found in other regions.
The surfperch is a large and flavorful fish, renowned for its culinary appeal, particularly in roasting.

Sweetfish are prized for their mild flavor and absence of a fishy smell, making them versatile for a variety of culinary preparations such as roasting, frying, or boiling. 

These fish are known to form schools and establish territories, often displaying aggressive behavior towards outsiders. This territorial nature can be exploited in fishing; by using a sweetfish as bait, other sweetfish may attack it, making them easier to catch.
Despite their adorable appearance, terrapins are renowned as a stamina-boosting delicacy, cherished by people of all ages. They are a prime target for professional fishers.
At first glance, it resembles a flatfish, but upon closer inspection, it's noticeably longer and thinner. When dried and grilled, it offers a delicious taste that is widely appreciated.
A type of salmon from the ocean, known for its delightfully chewy texture and exceptional taste.

The ussurian bullhead is typically found in the midstream and downstream sections of rivers, where the water is relatively clear and the riverbed consists of sand and mud. This species is known for its predatory diet, primarily feeding on fish eggs, larvae, shrimp, and smaller fish. The ussurian bullhead can reach a length of approximately 30 centimeters. While its appearance is similar to that of catfish, it is distinguished by its slender and elongated body.
Whitings are noted for their small, pointed snouts, which enable them to effectively locate prey hidden within the sand. They are predominantly found in areas rich in crustaceans.

The yellowfin sculpin is noted for its distinctive appearance, characterized by a short snout and broad dorsal fins.

These dorsal fins are equipped with numerous spines and soft rays, and it is said that laborers at the Extraction Mill enjoy a lighthearted pastime of betting on the number of spines a caught yellowfin sculpin will have.

A chordate in the flatfish family. Its body length measures at about 48cm with two eyes located on the right side.

A cold water fish that inhabits regions 400m below surface. It keeps close to the ocean floor for the majority of its lifetime.
An omnivore with a strong preference for flesh, especially shellfish. During spawning season, it swims up to the depth of below 100m to lay its eggs.
